opportunities.title: Small Research Grants
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Must have BES membership; open to researchers from all countries globally; projects can be conducted anywhere in the world. Not available for salary of principal researcher, bench fees, or hiring departmental vehicles. Not a scholarship; cannot fund projects forming part of a funded fellowship or undergraduate/master's degree.
opportunities.summary: Provides up to £5,000 for new and innovative ecological research of the highest international standard, with a clear ecological science focus.

opportunities.title: Synthesis Grants
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Main applicant must have BES membership (not required for all group members). Groups of 8-15 individuals with diverse mix of career stages, institutions and international participation, demonstrating EDI principles.
opportunities.summary: Fast-tracking innovative and impactful research by contributing up to £30k towards the formation of new two-year synthesis groups that bring together diverse interdisciplinary groups of 8-15 individuals to focus on data analysis and synthesis.

opportunities.title: Long-term Research Grants

amount.raw: £500 per year for 10 years; £3,500 claimable in year 1 (first 5 years), additional £3,500 in year 6

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Must have BES membership; open to all types of ecologists including conservation practitioners, reserve managers and consultants, as well as university academics; awarded to individuals, not organisations.
opportunities.summary: Provides small annual funding for 10 years to enable existing short-term projects with 1-2 years of data to be funded into the long term, supporting projects such as ecological restoration, habitat creation, control of alien species and climate change anywhere in the world.

opportunities.title: Pedagogical Research and Development Grants
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Must have BES membership; open to anyone involved in teaching ecology at any level (early years to lifelong learning, formal or informal settings), including industry; awarded to individuals, not organisations; projects max 12 months; funding unavailable for work forming part of a degree/masters/PhD/fellowship.
opportunities.summary: Funds research informing teaching and learning practices in ecology to improve learners' experience and promote excellence in teaching, e.g. evidence-based innovative practice, systematic reviews, exploring emerging education research areas.

opportunities.title: Connecting Ecologists with Other Disciplines Grants
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Must have BES membership; open to PhD students, postdoctoral fellows, early career ecologists, established researchers or employees of other organisations; must have employer/supervisor approval and a willing host organisation; undergraduates and masters students not eligible; awarded to individuals.
opportunities.summary: Promotes interdisciplinary skills by funding up to £20k towards placements (up to 12 months) in a different discipline or sector, immersing an ecologist in another professional world where ecology can make a difference.

opportunities.title: Outreach and Engagement Grants
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Lead applicant must have BES membership; open to individuals, teams and organisations across all experience levels; projects max 12 months; proposals aimed at non-academic audience; no restrictions on where applicants come from or where work is carried out.
opportunities.summary: Provides funding of up to £2,000 for individuals, teams and organisations to engage public audiences with the excitement, importance and relevance of ecological science through outreach, public engagement and science communication activities.

opportunities.title: Training and Travel Grants

amount.raw: max £250 for virtual conferences/courses; max £500 for in-person events

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Must be a BES member; must be a PhD student or postgraduate researcher (postdocs, undergraduates and masters students not eligible); must work/study at a university or research institution; must give a presentation if attending a meeting; must be at least three years since last awarded a BES training and travel grant.
opportunities.summary: Helps PhD students and postgraduate researchers meet the costs of specialist field training courses and the travel costs associated with presenting their work at workshops and conferences.

opportunities.title: Annual Meeting Grants 2026
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Must be a BES member; must be a citizen of and based in the Global South; must be travelling from and returning to the Global South country; must have applied to present at the Annual Meeting; must be at least three years since last awarded a BES Training and Travel Grant.
opportunities.summary: Supports researchers based in Global South countries to attend the BES Annual Meeting in the UK by funding travel from the applicant's country of residence to the UK and return, covering costs such as registration, transport, food and accommodation.
